sections.title: Russian Classics
sections.blurb: Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Turgenev, Gogol, Chekhov, and their contemporaries — often in several translations.

sections.title: English Classics
sections.blurb: Poets and novelists from Chaucer to the early modernists.

sections.title: Shakespeare
sections.blurb: The plays and poems on their own shelf.

sections.title: Classics of Western Civilisation
sections.blurb: Foundational works of Greece, Rome, and the European tradition — philosophy, history, and epic.

sections.title: American Classics
sections.blurb: Melville, Twain, Hawthorne, Poe, Whitman, Dickinson, James, Wharton, and the American canon.

sections.title: Continental Classics
sections.blurb: European masters in public-domain translation — Cervantes, Dumas, Hugo, Flaubert, Balzac, Zola, Goethe, Ibsen.

sections.title: World & Eastern Classics
sections.blurb: Foundational texts of the wider world — the Tao Te Ching, Analects, Bhagavad Gita, the Arabian Nights, the Rubáiyát, and more.

sections.title: Myth & Legend
sections.blurb: Gods, heroes, and folk tales — Bulfinch, the Eddas, Grimm, Andersen, Aesop, Beowulf.

sections.title: History
sections.blurb: Gibbon, Plutarch, Carlyle, Prescott, Parkman, and the great narrative historians.

sections.title: Science & Nature
sections.blurb: Darwin, Huxley, Faraday, Galileo, Euclid, and the literature of discovery.

sections.title: Children's Classics
sections.blurb: Peter Pan, The Wind in the Willows, Oz, Heidi, Pinocchio, Anne of Green Gables, and friends.
